author.name: Reliability Ruth
author.role: Develops the end-user applications and services that integrate ML models. Handles model deployment, configuration, and continuous monitoring of real-world performance. Employs feedback loops to facilitate iterative improvements and system reliability.

challenge.name: The Locked Shadow
challenge.description: A supplier contract for the next promotion week is already signed, and the team cannot deploy the new model without a shadow run to verify it. #reliability_ruth# demands a fully automated and governed shadow environment to protect the live forecast, while #automation_alex# insists on keeping it manual to avoid breaking the current pipeline stability.

output.content: I am not going to sign off on the new model deployment unless the shadow environment is fully governed. This is a hard line for me. If the shadow run is not governed, I will refuse to release the model to the live forecast service. I need to see the access controls and audit logs in place before I consider the deployment safe. There is no compromise on this point. The live forecast must be protected from any unverified changes. I will not accept a manual or partially automated setup as a substitute for proper governance. Until those controls are verified, the deployment stays blocked. I am not willing to risk the stability of the current pipeline for an uncontrolled release. This requirement is non negotiable.
output.reclassify_reason: The author explicitly defines the lack of full governance in the shadow environment as a hard line that will result in refusal to sign off, establishing a non-negotiable limit rather than a preference or trade-off.
